references.text: The people's original request to Aaron to make gods for them, which Aaron recounts here. The verse contains almost identical wording: 'Make us gods who can go before us.'
Describes the result of the people's demand—the golden calf was made and declared as the god who brought them out of Egypt.
Moses went up on the mountain and stayed there for forty days and forty nights, which explains the people's impatience and their statement that they did not know what had happened to him.
Moses' reflection on the sin of the golden calf, where he confirms that the people sinned by making a cast calf.
Stephen quotes this verse in his speech, recounting the people's words to Aaron about making gods who could go before them, since they did not know what had happened to Moses.
Stephen describes how the fathers would not obey Moses but pushed him away and turned their hearts back to Egypt.
The source verse illustrates the sin itself (abandoning God for other gods), while this verse explains the theological consequence of exactly that action.
This verse confirms and explains the theological consequence of the idolatry that began in the source verse.
